title: Compact keying policy generator and safe scaling procedure for KV hit stabilization
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: We have recurring customer complaints about token costs for chat workloads with high prefix skew. Existing prefix TTL heuristics reduce cost but cause bursts of increased origin load during rollout. Goal: build a compact keying policy generator that recommends per-prefix key consolidation rules and TTL tiers, produce hit-rate forecasts, and provide an automated safe-scaling procedure (shadow dry-run + staged rollforward) to apply the policy with rollback guarantees. Scope: - Input: sampling traces (prefix frequency, response length, batching characteristics, KV hit latency) - Output: policy file (key canonicalization rules, TTL per tier, batching hint) + per-prefix forecast table and risk score - Safety: staged canary with shadow replay, automatic reversion triggers, and cost/latency guardrails Acceptance criteria: 1) Policy generator produces per-prefix TTL recommendations that increase expected cache hit-rate by >= 8% on held-out traces with <= 1.5% expected tail-latency increase. 2) Safe-scaling procedure can revert a policy within 5 minutes automatically on guardrail violations. 3) Tool integrates with console rollout UI and emits telemetry for per-key hit delta and rollback events. Success metrics: - Delta in served tokens from cache and origin - End-to-end P95 inference latency on canary routes - Number of automatic rollbacks during internal pilot Plan: 1) Design generator: heuristic + probabilistic hit-model (mixture of exponential inter-arrival and Zipf prefix popularity) and cheap Monte Carlo simulator for candidate policies. 2) Implement canonicalization rules engine that groups low-cardinality affixes and supports suffix-stripping and token-window bucketing. 3) Integrate batching hints: recommend batch-size targets and max-latency budget per prefix class. 4) Build rollout harness: shadow-run, canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with automated rollforward only if simulated hitlift and live guardrails pass for 30m windows. 5) Internal pilot across 3 customers and synthetic workloads, then gradual rollout. Risks and mitigation: - Over-canonicalization may reduce cache usefulness for high-cardinality prefixes. Mitigation: conservative compression threshold + sample-based backtests. - Burst origin spikes on revert: pre-warm and controlled ramp-down + autoscale reserve. - Telemetry lag: push immediate aggregate counters (per-prefix hit/miss, origin-QPS) with 1s granularity for canaries. Docs and artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/CPG-Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6421 simulation notebook: https://drive.google.com/sim_cpg_v1 Notes: this ticket focuses on the recommendation generator and the safe apply mechanism; a separate follow-up will be created for console rollout polish and RBAC audit integration.
